requirement: Cache normalized price lookups per instance without caching failures, and provide a spy helper that records calls to a real method while keeping its behavior.
skeleton: PriceBook with a copied table and per-instance cache, lookup raising LookupError, price normalizing and caching, total summing; spy_on contextmanager checking callability and wrapping with patch.object wraps.
caption: Caching verified with a spy built from unittest.mock.patch.object and wraps. PriceBook copies its price table on construction and keeps a per-instance cache created in __init__. lookup(sku) is the slow authoritative path and raises LookupError naming an unknown sku. price(sku) strips and uppercases the sku, calls lookup only when that key is not cached yet, stores the result and returns it; a LookupError is raised before anything is stored, so unknown skus are retried. total(skus) sums price over the skus. spy_on(obj, name) is a contextlib.contextmanager that reads the attribute, raises TypeError saying the name is not callable for plain data, and otherwise enters patch.object(obj, name, wraps=original), yielding a MagicMock that records every call yet forwards it to the real bound method and returns its real result. On exit the instance attribute is removed and the class method shows through again. The fixture asserts that pricing a1, padded A1, b2 and A1 totals 850 with lookup calls exactly A1 then B2, that the spy returns the real 100 for B2, that an unknown z9 raises LookupError on both attempts with two lookups, that the patch appears in vars during the block and not after, that a second book's cache is separate from the first's, that later edits to the caller's table are not seen, and that spying on _table raises TypeError.

plan.intent: Prove a cache avoids repeat lookups
constraints: Each normalized sku is looked up once per instance
Unknown skus raise LookupError and are not cached
The spy forwards to the real method and returns its result
Caches and tables are not shared with other instances or the caller
Spying on a non-callable raises TypeError
The spy is removed after the block

rationale.teaches: patch.object(obj, name, wraps=original) records calls while the real code still runs, so call counts can prove caching without faking data.
rationale.why: Replacing the method with a plain mock returns MagicMocks and tests nothing real, while not spying at all leaves the cache unverified.

ops.docstring: Spy on a real method with patch.object(wraps=...) to count calls, not fake them.

candidates.why_wrong: Without wraps the spy returns MagicMocks instead of calling the real lookup.
Skus are not normalized, so case and padding variants miss the cache or the table.
The cache is a class attribute shared by every PriceBook instance.
Data attributes are wrapped as if they were methods instead of raising TypeError.
The caller's dict is kept by reference, so later edits change prices.
